This. This application. Okay. City administration received an application from Dream on Limited Corp to amend the Willows residential and golf course community concept plan, which was initially adopted in 2003.

The proposed amendments primarily affect the western portion of the neighborhood, which is the second phase of the development and includes amendments to the official community plan and zoning bylaw to ensure consistency between these documents.
These images represent a comparison between the adopted landies plan, the left image and the proposed amendment on the right.
Notable changes include number one, a general reconfiguration of the street and lot layout of the western half of the development.
Number two, the addition of 6.4 hectares into the concept plan area, which accommodates an additional 7.4 hectares in the northern portion of the neighborhood.
Number three, introduction of an area for a hotel and spa. Number four, introduction of municipal reserve.
Number five, a new south access to clearance avenue. In addition to this, the amendment will allow for fee sample lots to be accommodated.
And the changes allow for an increased build out population increase from 1557 to 200396, which is approximately 839.
In 2001, Dream submitted an application to amend the Willows concept plan, which was ultimately refused by council due to the large number of questions concerns and opposition received.
To address concerns, the applicant worked with the residents of the neighborhood to revise the initial amendment plan prior to finalization and submission of this application.
This consultation included 14 in person and virtual meetings, which were held in June and July of 2022.
Upon receiving the application, development reviews solicited comment from the public.
Details of the application, including a video presentation by administration and dream, was posted on the city's engage page, which continues to be updated as the file progresses.
The first public notice was mailed to all property owners within the Willows on March 3 followed by public open house held on March 22.
72 individuals signed the attendance sheet at the open house while nine filled out comment sheets.

Through the review, a total of eight written responses were received along with three phone calls. During public consultation, the following were noted as positive changes from dreams 2021 application.

Dream's public engagement and revisions to the plan from the previous submission, the new location of the hotel in Spa, removal of a road connecting phase 2 to the Cartwright Street roundabout, the proposal for the south access road onto Clarence and the installation of additional walking paths.
The following concerns were also noted.

Any quality of taxation between future fee simple lots and existing bareland condominium units, a decrease in property values, due to an increase in density and development, the need for additional sidewalks and pathways and select locations, which led to several changes during the review process.

The need for more centralized park space, which also led to additional MR being included in the plan, and increases in traffic and noise and opposition to the proposed south access road onto Clarence Avenue.
This slide provides comparison between the proposed land use plan in 2021 and today's proposal. Please note following items.
Number one, the revised hotel in Spa location away from existing residential areas.
Removal of the commercial neighborhood node, which is now replaced with low and medium density multi-unit dwellings.
Removal of a proposed medium density multi-unit dwelling group in the red barn area, which is now proposed to be used for an amenity area.
Number four, inclusion of additional sidewalks, crosswalks, and traffic calming along Cartwright Street.
Five, new south, a new south, all direction access to Clarence Avenue.
Six, removal of the road connection from phase two to the Cartwright Street roundabout.
Seven, all direction access to lower an avenue, which was previously right in the left out, I believe.
Number eight, additional municipal reserve added in a more centralized location.
The proposed OCP map amendment is also required for the purpose of including the north development area within the boundary of the willows neighborhood.
In addition, a text amendment to the OCP is required to accommodate for a hotel in Spa.
Map and text amendments are also proposed to the city zoning by law.

A map of amendment is required to resume the north development area from DAG-1, which was an agricultural district in place prior to the city's municipal boundary alteration to DCD-4, which is consistent with the remainder of the neighborhood.
Text amendments are also required, including but not limited to provisions to accommodate fee simple residential lots.
Production and minimum site widths and areas for one unit dwellings and the inclusion of development standards for hotels and accessor uses.

In conclusion, development review recommends that a copy of this report be submitted to city council recommending that city council consider the proposed amendments to the willows residential golf course community concept plan, the official community plan and the zoning by lobby approved.
